title: Give each screen a waiting list it can rearrange

blocks.text: A clinic's front desk keeps one `Waitlist`. Several screens show it: the lobby screen sorts the names alphabetically and hides some of them for privacy; each nurse's screen takes the next few patients and adds walk-ins by hand. The desk reports two problems. After the lobby screen refreshes, patients are called in alphabetical order instead of the order they arrived, and some are missing from the queue. And a nurse's screen sometimes crashes when a new patient checks in at the desk, while on a quiet morning it crashes as soon as the nurse adds a walk-in.
`Waitlist` already tracks who checks in and who is called in. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Waitlist.java`:

items: `waiting()`: the list a screen gets of everyone waiting, in arrival order;
`next(count)`: the list a nurse's screen gets of the first `count` patients.

blocks.text: When you're done, a screen can sort, trim and add to whatever list it got without changing the queue, and its list stays as it was when it took it. About three lines in total.

cases.says: waiting() lists everyone still waiting in arrival order, and next(n) the first n of them, or all if fewer wait
sorting and removing names from the list waiting() returned leaves the waitlist's own order and size unchanged
a list next(n) returned still holds the same patients, and can still be read, after others check in or are called in
a list next(n) returned can be added to even when it is empty, and adding to it does not touch the waitlist

origin.section: A Returned Collection Is Whatever the Caller Can Do With It

concepts: A method that returns its internal collection gives every caller write access to it; returning a copy keeps the caller's changes, and later changes to the owner, apart.
A method returns the same kind of collection on every path, so an empty result is as editable as a full one.
